network_1_local_isp.note: same pseudonym as every earlier unforged request from this network (ip:650ecd10c6f2b575:* buckets); earlier wave matched it to HMAC(public IP of this network)

network_2_supabase_pg_net.origin: staging DB (uzeagzcyvxzrpjgrhaql, sa-east-1) via net.http_get, pg_net 0.19.5

conclusion: Two distinct networks produce two distinct, stable buckets (650ecd.. vs 4bd80e..): client_ip is per origin, not a shared edge/proxy IP.

Within each network the key is invariant to forged X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP and even a forged X-Vercel-Forwarded-For (3 pg_net requests with different/absent forged values -> one key, count 3): the platform overwrites x-vercel-forwarded-for with the real peer and the app ignores the spoofable headers.

The key is not HMAC of any forged value, of the Vercel edge IPs, of the DB server IPv6 (staging host has no AAAA, so pg_net egresses over Supabase IPv4 NAT), of 127.0.0.1 or of the 'unknown' fallback.

Limitation: the literal IPv4 egress of pg_net cannot be read from Postgres or Vercel runtime logs (no IP field) without a third-party IP echo, which was out of scope; identity is proven differentially.
cleanup: authfail buckets expire with their 900 s window; no schema change; pg_net requests only to the staging URL
